passage:
Monday. At lunch, Jatin opened the class chat and found a photo of himself mid-stumble on sports day, with cruel comments under it. His hands went cold and he wanted to disappear. He did not reply. He took screenshots of the photo and the names, then put the phone away.
Tuesday. Still feeling sick, Jatin walked into Chaitanya Sir's room before first bell and showed him the screenshots. "This is not your fault," Chaitanya Sir said, and stayed beside Jatin while calling the school's safeguarding lead. She arrived within the hour, copied the screenshots and said the school would deal with the sharing. Jatin blocked the accounts and reported the post.
The following Monday the photo was gone, the safeguarding lead had checked in twice, and Jatin ate lunch with two classmates.

qa.q: What did Jatin do with the photo and the names before putting the phone away?
qa.a: Jatin took screenshots of the photo and the names.

qa.q: How did Jatin feel when finding the photo, and what shows it?
qa.a: Exposed and helpless; the cold hands and the wish to disappear show it, and Jatin did not reply.

qa.q: Which step turned things around, and why?
qa.a: Showing the screenshots to Chaitanya Sir before first bell, because an adult could reassure Jatin and pass it to the safeguarding lead the same day.

qa.q: What might Chaitanya Sir have seen in Jatin walking in that early?
qa.a: A student who was upset but brave enough to ask for help, which is why Chaitanya Sir stayed close and said it was not Jatin's fault.

grounding: A teenager finds a photo shared with cruel comments and uses evidence, a trusted adult, reporting and blocking.

passage: Gurpreet, put the phone down a minute. When I was fifteen there was a clip of me falling off the stage at our school farewell, and an older class shared it with laughing comments. My face burned as if the whole town had watched. My hands shook, but I remembered to save pictures of the comments before doing anything else. Then I told my mother, standing in the kitchen with the phone still in my hand. She hugged me first and said it was in no way my fault. That same evening she phoned the principal, who listened, took the pictures I had saved and promised action. By the next day the clip was down, and I had blocked those accounts. I still remember how light I felt walking into school after. Nandini

qa.q: What did Nandini fall off at the school farewell?
qa.a: Nandini fell off the stage at the school farewell.

qa.q: How did Nandini feel on seeing the clip, and what shows it?
qa.a: Ashamed and exposed; the burning face and the shaking hands show it.

qa.q: What did young Nandini do before anything else, and why did it help?
qa.a: Nandini saved pictures of the comments first, which gave the principal proof to act on.

qa.q: How might Nandini's mother have felt hearing the news in the kitchen?
qa.a: Worried and protective; hugging first and saying it was not Nandini's fault shows care before action.

grounding: A teenager finds a clip shared with cruel comments and saves evidence, tells a trusted adult, and the school acts.
